title: SelfDescription
description: A person's own account of themselves, written once for every occasion: who they are, what they are looking for in their work, what they enjoy outside it, what they can offer others, and what is coming up — in their own language, in the first person, as a structured text with headings. It is GENERAL, not about one event: an application that introduces people (at a conference, a business meeting, a trip) reads it as context and decides for itself what is relevant to the occasion. ONE LIVE RECORD PER PERSON, on THEIR OWN vault; a later interview replaces it. HOW THE TEXT CAME TO BE MATTERS AND IS RECORDED: it is usually composed by an application from an interview — spoken or written answers to questions — into text that reads as if the person had written it in one go, without the questions, and the person then reads it, corrects it and approves it before it is stored. So the text is the person's APPROVED statement, not their verbatim words; `provenance` says so, and `approvedAt` is when they approved it. Nothing in it should be read as more than they approved. Not a profile card: name, picture and contact details stay in the person's `User` / `ProfessionalProfile` records; this is the narrative those do not have room for. Checked before minting (2026-11-15): the registry has no such type; in the known set, `User.bio` and `ProfessionalProfile.bio` are fields of profiles other applications own and edit, and `Summary` summarises conversations.

id.description: Stable application id, unchanged when the record is replaced by a later version.

authorEName.description: Whose self-description this is. Always the owner of the vault it is on.

language.description: BCP 47 tag of the language the text is written in, e.g. `nl`, `de`, `lb`, `sr-Latn`.

text.description: The whole text as Markdown: `##` headings for sections, `###` for subsections, lists where the person listed things. Readable as plain text by anything that does not render Markdown.

sections.description: The same text cut at its `##` headings, each part labelled with what it is about, so a reader can find 'what they are looking for' without understanding the language. `kind` is an open vocabulary: `about` (who they are, background, current work), `seeking` (whom or what they are looking for, mostly work), `interests` (life outside work: hobbies, sport, passions), `offering` (what others can come to them for), `plans` (trips, events, dates coming up), `other`. A reader that meets an unknown `kind` treats it as `other`. Concatenating the `markdown` of all sections, in order, gives `text`.

audience.description: Who the author MEANT this for, in words; the ACL decides who may read the record, and where the two disagree the ACL wins. `introductions` — the author plus the application that captured it, which may show parts of it to people it introduces the author to; `self` — the author alone; an application may use it to advise the author and must never show it to anybody else. Unknown value: treat as `self`.

provenance.description: How the text came to be, in the ecosystem's `{app, auto, generatedAt}` shape. `auto: true` with `source: "interview"` means an application composed the text from the person's answers; `mode` is `voice` or `text`. `approvedAt` is when the person read and approved it — the record is not written before that.
